title: Set USB channel constraints for the selected generation
summary: Obtain the selected USB generation and device channel requirements before assigning impedance, skew and length constraints.
applies_to: USB data channels; the source includes USB 2.0 and SuperSpeed guidance.
verification: Read back net rules and inspect the complete channel against device requirements.
limitations: Do not transfer limits between generations or use a generic trace width.

title: Avoid unnecessary branches on USB data pairs
summary: Keep unused branches and test-point stubs out of high-speed USB data paths; account for discontinuities in the channel review.
required_inputs: Channel topology and device layout guidance
verification: Inspect routing and test-point connections for branches.
limitations: This does not authorize adding AC coupling to USB 2.0 or cover Type-C power negotiation.

title: Place CAN termination at the bus ends
summary: For a conventional high-speed CAN bus, terminate its physical ends and keep node branches electrically short. Match termination to the intended cable.
required_inputs: Full bus topology and node positions
verification: Check endpoint termination count and observe bus waveforms at remote nodes.
limitations: The cited classical CAN guide does not establish CAN FD timing or every CAN physical-layer variant.

citations.locator: Sections 4.5 and 4.8, Line Termination and Stubs

title: Evaluate split termination for CAN common-mode noise
summary: Evaluate split termination when common-mode noise needs attenuation. Keep the network balanced and consider its reference connection.
applies_to: High-speed CAN endpoints using an appropriate split-termination topology.
verification: Measure common-mode noise and confirm differential signal margins.
limitations: Split termination is an option, not an instruction to populate it at every node.

title: Review RS-485 termination and stub delay
summary: For transmission-line operation, match endpoint termination to the cable and assess stubs against driver transition time.
applies_to: RS-485 bus trunks with attached nodes.
verification: Inspect endpoint loads and measure reflections at the furthest nodes.
limitations: Bit rate alone cannot set a permitted stub length.

citations.locator: Section 6, Bus Termination and Stub Length

title: Include failsafe bias in the RS-485 load budget
summary: Check receiver behavior on an idle or disconnected bus. Include external bias and termination in the driver load budget.
applies_to: RS-485 networks needing a defined receiver idle state.
verification: Calculate worst-case idle margin and driven load.
limitations: Bias values depend on the complete bus; internal failsafe capabilities vary.

title: Check RS-485 ground potential and common-mode range
summary: Assess remote ground differences against receiver limits. Consider signal and supply isolation when the installation requires it.
applies_to: RS-485 links spanning independently powered equipment.
verification: Review the full reference-current path and common-mode budget.
limitations: This is not insulation coordination or a prescription for a ground resistor.

title: Calculate the I2C pull-up resistance window
summary: Bound pull-up resistance using bus rise time and the weakest permitted sink current. Include effective parallel pull-ups.
applies_to: Open-drain I2C modes covered by UM10204 Section 7.1.
verification: Calculate resistance bounds and measure rise time and low voltage.
limitations: A customary resistor value is not evidence of compliance; push-pull variants differ.

title: Review I2C capacitance before adding buffers
summary: When capacitance is excessive, assess speed reduction or segmentation. Buffer delay and voltage offsets become part of each segment budget.
verification: Recalculate each segment and verify logic levels and timing.
limitations: A buffer is not transparent; follow its connection restrictions.

title: Preserve Ethernet MDI pair geometry
summary: Derive MDI trace geometry from the stackup and PHY requirements. Maintain pair symmetry through bends and layer transitions.
applies_to: Twisted-pair Ethernet PHY-to-magnetics paths; source targets SMSC devices.
verification: Inspect pair geometry, reference continuity and transition symmetry.
limitations: Do not reuse source-specific dimensions across PHY families or Ethernet variants.

citations.locator: Section 3.1, Controlled Impedance for Differential Signals, pages 6-7

title: Evaluate series termination on Ethernet MAC-side signals
summary: Consider source-side series termination for MAC interface ringing or emissions, with an uninterrupted reference path.
applies_to: MII/RMII connections consistent with the selected PHY and MAC.
verification: Check receiver timing and waveforms with the proposed resistor.
limitations: AN18.6 example values are device-specific and are not RGMII timing guidance.

title: Respect the Ethernet magnetics isolation boundary
summary: Review copper and reference regions on both sides of Ethernet magnetics against the selected PHY, connector and isolation design.
applies_to: Transformer-isolated Ethernet; the source layout is LAN9512/LAN9513/LAN9514.
verification: Inspect all copper layers and components across the intended boundary.
limitations: This family-specific layout is not a universal plane-splitting rule or safety-clearance calculation.
